t.3.53.1: Bṛhadaśva said: Having bowed to the gods, she smiled and said to Nala, “Show me your love as you wish, O king; what shall I do for you?”
t.3.53.2: I myself, and whatever other wealth I have, all of it is yours; with full trust, my lord, show me your love.
t.3.53.3: That message of the swans, O king, burns me, for it is on your account, O hero, that the kings have been assembled here by me.
t.3.53.4: If you reject me, who am devoted to you, O giver of honor, I shall resort to poison, fire, water, or the rope because of you.
t.3.53.5: Thus addressed by the princess of Vidarbha, Nala replied to her: "While the guardians of the worlds are present, how can you desire a mere man?"
t.3.53.6: Let your mind turn to those great-souled lords, the makers of the worlds, to the dust of whose feet I am not equal.
t.3.53.7: For a mortal who does what is displeasing to the gods meets his death. Save me, O lady of faultless limbs, and choose those foremost of the gods!
t.3.53.8: Then Damayantī of the pure smile, slowly uttering words made faint with tears, spoke to King Nala.
t.3.53.10: You yourself, O best of men, and the gods led by Agni, let all come together to the place where my svayaṃvara is to be held.
t.3.53.9: There is a means that I have seen, O lord of men, one free from harm, by which no fault will fall upon you in any way, O king.
t.3.53.11: Then, O lord of men, in the presence of the world-guardians I shall choose you, O tiger among men; in this way no fault will arise.
t.3.53.12: Thus addressed by Vaidarbhī, O lord of the people, King Nala came back to the place where the gods were assembled.
t.3.53.13: The world-guardians, lords all together, saw him coming thus, and having seen him, they then asked him about everything that had happened.
t.3.53.14: The gods said: "Did you see Damayantī of the bright smile, O king? And what did she say to all of us? Tell us, O sinless lord of the earth."
t.3.53.15: Commanded by you, I entered Damayantī's dwelling, which had very great courtyards and was guarded by aged staff-bearing doorkeepers.
t.3.53.16: And as I entered there, no man saw me except that daughter of the king, through the power of you yourselves alone.
t.3.53.17: Her friends were seen by me, and I too was noticed by them; and on seeing me, O lords of the gods, they were all astonished.
t.3.53.18: And even while I was describing you, O best of gods, the fair-faced one, her mind already set on me, chooses me alone.
t.3.53.19: And the maiden said to me: “Let the gods come, all together with you, O best of men, to the place where my svayaṃvara is to be held.”
t.3.53.20: In their presence I shall choose you, O best of men; in this way, O mighty-armed one, no fault will fall upon you.
t.3.53.21: This, O gods, is all that happened, and I have related it in full; but you, lords of the thirty gods, are the authority.
